EVM performance is important, but at the moment pure computational performance is not the main bottleneck (though it probably holds the second place). The top performance bottleneck is state (accounts, storage) access (reading & writing). That's why efforts like improved DB layout in Erigon are so important (https://github.com/ledgerwatch/erigon#key-features). For potential future improvements see Vitalik's https://hackmd.io/@vbuterin/state_expiry_paths Thanks! That's helpful. Besides improved DB layout, is there also some caching being done in Ethereum nodes typically? There must be some state that is accessed exponentially more often than other, no? Yes, typically Ethereum nodes cache hot data

excerpts.author: yperbasis
excerpts.content: EVM performance is important, but at the moment pure computational performance is not the main bottleneck (though it probably holds the second place). The top performance bottleneck is state (accounts, storage) access (reading & writing). That's why efforts like improved DB layout in Erigon are so important (https://github.com/ledgerwatch/erigon#key-features). For potential future improvements see Vitalik's https://hackmd.io/@vbuterin/state_expiry_paths
